CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes

n
  April 14, 2025-5:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber
  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmember Jones)

  CLOSED SESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:01 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session items:

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  Councilmember Jones  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  arrived at 5:16 p.m.  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Name of Case: Protich v. City of Pasadena, et al.
  Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No.: 22AHCV01222

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Name of Case: Harrell, C. v. City of Pasadena
  Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No.: 20STCV06887

  The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
(
  action at this time.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:05
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Lyon.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison (via teleconference)
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  Councilmember Madison reported that he is participating remotely
  under the "just cause" provision of the Brown Act on the basis of
  medical illness and stated that no one over 18 years of age is in the
  room with him.

  Council Minutes  1  04/14/2025
 CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo and Councilmember Jones presented a certificate of
  recognition to the Pasadena High School football team for their
  tremendous athletic efforts and securing the GIF Southern Section
  title. Mayor Gordo also recognized Principal Eric Barba, Assistant
  Principal Brian Lanagan, Athletics Director Seth Pettit, Coach Ron
  Jones, and Coach Dejuan Shamburger, and thanked them for their
  hard work and dedication to the team.

  Mayor Gordo announced April 2025 as Sexual Assault Prevention
  and Awareness Month, and encouraged everyone to participate in
  Denim Day on April 30, 2025 by wearing jeans, and presented a
  proclamation to Maura Harrington, Vice Chair of the Commission on
  the Status of Women (CSW), Jill Thompson, CSW District 3  I

  Commissioner, and Leticia Lopez, CSW Staff, who accepted the
  proclamation on behalf of the Commission, thanked the City Council
  for the recognition, and emphasized the importance of addressing
  the underlying issues of sexual assault and raising awareness.

  Councilmember Lyon requested that the meeting be adjourned in
  memory of Dr. Edward C. Stone, a project scientist for the Voyager
  program and former Director at Jet Propulsions Laboratory. He
  spoke on Dr. Stone's significant contributions to science and the
  surrounding community as a physics professor at Caltech.

  Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting also be adjourned in
  memory of Doug Kranwinkle, longtime Pasadena resident and public
  figure, and spoke on his various contributions throughout his law
  career, especially during the Civil Rights era, and his commitment to
  Pasadena through numerous organizations and public service
  positions he held.

  Mayor Gordo also requested that the meeting be adjourned in
  memory of Jim Ukropina, and spoke on his many accomplishments
  in corporate governance, his contributions to the City of Pasadena,
  and throughout his professional life.

  Lastly, Mayor Gordo proclaimed April 24, 2025, as Day of
  Remembrance of the Armenian Genocide in the City of Pasadena,
  noting the importance of joining the Armenian community to
  memorialize this moment in history and acknowledging their fallen
  ancestors.

  Councilmember Jones requested for April 15, 2025 to be
  commemorated as Jackie Robinson Day, and noted the significance
  of Jackie Robinson breaking racial barriers in Major League
  Baseball, and his importance to the history and culture of Pasadena.

Council Minutes  2  04/14/2025
 PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Isabella Llyod-Damnjanovic, Pasadena resident, inquired about the
MATTERS NOT ON THE  City's resources available to unhoused individuals during summer
AGENDA  heatwaves and advocated for the City to include environmental
  justice initiatives in the plans for open space and conservation,
  climate action, and public health.

  Joe Colletti, Pasadena resident, provided historical information on
  Dr. Thomas B. Elliot, and advocated for the City Council to
  commemorate those who founded and were first to name this region
  "Pasadena."

  The following individuals provided comments advocating for the
  City's divestment from specific companies (in relation to Israel) and
  the Fire & Police Retirement Board pension portfolios:

  Michael Flynn, Pasadena resident
  Dylan Banner, Pasadena resident
  Randall Heyn-Lamb, Pasadena resident

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, requested that the City's
  underground utility project be agendized for discussion and provided
  comments on the oversight of the City's Police Department.

  The following individuals advocated for rent relief programs to aid
  residents impacted by the Eaton Fire:

  Shayna Reed, Altadena resident
  Gil Barel, Pasadena resident

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, requested the City Council agendize
  discussion of the City's response to the Eaton Fire.

  Kimberly Douglas, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns over the
  federal government's recent deportation of Maryland resident,
  Kilmar Abrego Garcia.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Madison disclosed
  that his law firm represents Mr. Kilmar Abrego Garcia.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Hampton
  suggested commemorating the City's founders and history in the
  Central Library once renovations and retrofits are completed.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Jones noted that the
  City's undergrounding project is to be discussed at an upcoming
  Municipal Services Committee meeting and is also listed as a project
  under the City's Capital Improvement Project budget.

Council Minutes  3  04/14/2025
   In response to public comment, City staff reported that the matter of
  the oversight of the City's Police Department is scheduled to be
  discussed at the next Public Safety Committee meeting.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Cole supported the
  idea of the Finance Committee reviewing the City's investment
  policy.

Council Minutes  11  04/14/2025
   MOTION:  Councilmember Cole advocated for directing the City Manager to
  work with the Housing Department and the Rent Stabilization
  Department to establish a centralized rental assistance resource, to
  assist tenants directly affected by the Eaton Fire, as defined under
  the City's Affirmative Defense Ordinance, working collaboratively
  with the Pasadena Community Foundation to identify one or more
  nonprofits to provide assistance and to minimize evictions through
  mediation and rental assistance with tenants and their landlords, with
  potential consideration of City matching funds, as well as setting up
  a reporting mechanism for those who seek relief under the City's
  ordinance, available to both tenants and their landlords.

  City Manager Marquez reported that any potential matching funds
  from the City's general fund would need to be part of the City's
  budget process. He cautioned that given economic uncertainties and
  potential cuts in federal funding, such funds are not readily available.
  City staff is thoroughly reviewing the entire proposed budget to
  determine what resources exist for matching dollars.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the proposed
  motion (as part of an information item) and offered the following
  substitute motion:

  It was moved by Councilmember Madison to direct the City Manager
  to return with a positioned proposal, in line with the City Council's
  discussion, for consideration by the City Council. (Substitute motion
  failed due to lack of second)

  AMENDED MOTION:  Following direction, it was moved by Councilmember Cole,
  seconded by Councilmember Hampton, to direct the City Manager to
  develop the best way to work with the Pasadena Community
  Foundation and other community partners to set up an effective
  resource for meeting the needs of tenants affected by the Eaton Fire,
  under the terms of the City's Affirmative Defense Ordinance,
  available to both tenants and landlords for assistance.
